question:
What actions did Vijayalaya Chola take after capturing the Kaveri delta?
I. He established the town of Thanjavur.
II. He built a temple for the goddess Nishumbhasudini.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vijayalaya Chola (विजयालय चोल) was the founder of the Imperial (Medieval) Chola dynasty around 850 CE, rising as a feudatory of the Pallavas.

• After capturing the Kaveri (Cauvery) delta, he founded and established the town/city of Thanjavur (तंजावुर), which became the Chola capital.

• He also built a temple there dedicated to the goddess Nishumbhasudini (Durga), so both statements I and II are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Cholas were revived by Vijayalaya after the decline of the earlier Sangam-age Cholas.

• The dynasty reached its zenith under Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, famous for the Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur.

• The Cholas are noted for their strong navy, local self-government and Dravidian temple architecture.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as it excludes the correct fact that he also built the Nishumbhasudini temple.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as it excludes his founding of Thanjavur, which is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are historically true.

question: Which Rajputs refused to accept the authority of the Mughals for a long time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sisodiya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sisodiya (सिसोदिया) Rajputs of Mewar (Udaipur) refused to accept Mughal authority for a very long time and resisted their expansion.

• Rana Sanga and later Maharana Pratap of the Sisodia clan were the fiercest opponents of the Mughals, unlike many other Rajput houses that allied through matrimonial ties.

• Maharana Pratap fought Akbar's forces at the Battle of Haldighati (1576) and never fully submitted.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mewar finally reached an accord with the Mughals under Rana Amar Singh I and Emperor Jahangir in 1615.

• The Sisodias traced descent from the Guhilot dynasty and were considered the most prestigious Rajput lineage.

• Their capital shifted from Chittorgarh to Udaipur, founded by Udai Singh II.

NOTE

• Rathore (Option 1): Rajput clan of Marwar (Jodhpur) and Bikaner; many entered Mughal service.

• Kachhwaha (Option 2): Rajputs of Amber/Jaipur who allied with the Mughals through marriage (e.g., Raja Man Singh).

• Chauhan (Option 3): Ancient Rajput dynasty of Ajmer/Delhi, famed for Prithviraj Chauhan, predating strong Mughal-era resistance.

question: 'AI Kiran' in India is a pioneering initiative co-led by the ________.
option_1: Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser
option_4: National Association of Software and Service Companies
solution_text:
The correct answer is Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'AI Kiran' (ए.आई. किरण) is a pioneering initiative launched in 2025 to empower and champion women in Artificial Intelligence leadership in India.

• It is co-led by the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India, in collaboration with industry and community partners.

• The movement aims to bring around one million women into the AI ecosystem.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The initiative is associated with technology leader Kirthiga Reddy (former Meta India head).

• The current Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India is Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood.

• The PSA office also coordinates India's AI policy and cross-ministry science and technology efforts.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog (Option 2): The premier policy think-tank of India; not the co-lead of AI Kiran.

• Confederation of Indian Industry (Option 3): A leading industry association, not the initiative's co-lead.

• National Association of Software and Service Companies (Option 4): NASSCOM, the IT-industry body; not the co-leader of AI Kiran.

question: What is the minimum annual contribution (in Rs.) required to open and maintain an NPS Vatsalya account launched in September 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NPS Vatsalya (एन.पी.एस. वात्सल्य) is a pension scheme for minors launched in September 2024, allowing parents/guardians to invest for a child's future.

• The minimum contribution to open the account is Rs. 1,000, and a minimum of Rs. 1,000 per year is required to maintain the account.

• There is no upper limit on the contribution amount.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme is regulated by the PFRDA (Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority).

• On the child attaining 18 years, the account converts into a regular NPS (Tier-I) account.

• It was announced in the Union Budget 2024-25 by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

NOTE

• 500 (Option 1): Not the prescribed minimum annual contribution for NPS Vatsalya.

• 2500 (Option 3): Incorrect figure; exceeds the actual Rs. 1,000 minimum.

• No minimum limit (Option 4): Incorrect, as a minimum annual contribution of Rs. 1,000 is mandatory.

question:
Which of the following is one of the parameters of Financial Inclusion Index in India?
I. Access
II. Usage
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Financial Inclusion Index (वित्तीय समावेशन सूचकांक) is published by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to measure the extent of financial inclusion across the country.

• It is built on three broad parameters: Access, Usage and Quality, so both Access (I) and Usage (II) are valid parameters.

• The index ranges from 0 to 100, where 0 means complete financial exclusion and 100 means full inclusion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The three parameters carry weights of Access 35%, Usage 45% and Quality 20%.

• The index was first published by RBI in August 2021 for the period ending March 2021.

• It has no 'base year' and reflects cumulative efforts of stakeholders over the years.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete; Usage is also a parameter.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete; Access is also a parameter.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both Access and Usage are recognised parameters.

question: What is India's position in the World Press Freedom Index 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 151st.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the World Press Freedom Index 2025 (वर्ल्ड प्रेस फ्रीडम सूचकांक), India was ranked 151st out of 180 countries, with a score of about 32.96.

• This was an improvement of 8 places from its 159th rank in 2024, yet still in the 'very serious' category.

• The index is released annually by Reporters Without Borders (RSF).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Norway topped the 2025 index, followed by Estonia and the Netherlands.

• The index evaluates the political, economic, legislative, social and security context for journalists.

• 2025 marked World Press Freedom Day themes around media independence and safety of journalists.

NOTE

• 169th (Option 1): Not India's 2025 rank.

• 102nd (Option 2): Incorrect; far higher than India's actual position.

• 132nd (Option 3): Incorrect; India's rank was 151st, not 132nd.

question: The Export Preparedness Index in India is based on how many pillars?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Export Preparedness Index (निर्यात तैयारी सूचकांक) is released by NITI Aayog to assess the export readiness of Indian States and UTs.

• It is based on four pillars: Policy, Business Ecosystem, Export Ecosystem and Export Performance.

• These four pillars are further divided into multiple sub-pillars and indicators.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first EPI was released in 2020; subsequent editions include 2021, 2022 and 2024.

• In EPI 2024, top-performing States included Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

• The index helps identify challenges and opportunities to boost India's export competitiveness.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 1): Incorrect; the EPI uses four, not two, pillars.

• 6 (Option 3): Incorrect number of pillars.

• 8 (Option 4): Incorrect; there are four pillars, not eight.

question: The World Wetlands Day 2025 was celebrated at which of the following place of Uttar Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gonda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The national-level World Wetlands Day 2025 (विश्व आर्द्रभूमि दिवस) was celebrated at the Parvati Arga Ramsar Site in Gonda district, Uttar Pradesh.

• The theme for 2025 was 'Protecting Wetlands for our Common Future'.

• World Wetlands Day is observed every year on 2 February, marking the signing of the Ramsar Convention in 1971.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was signed in Ramsar, Iran, in 1971.

• India had 89 Ramsar sites (the highest in Asia) around this period, with Uttar Pradesh holding the most among States.

• Parvati Arga is a bird sanctuary and an important wetland habitat.

NOTE

• Prayagraj (Option 1): A city in UP known for the Triveni Sangam and Kumbh Mela; not the 2025 venue.

• Kanpur (Option 2): An industrial city on the Ganga; not the celebration site.

• Varanasi (Option 4): A holy city on the Ganga; not where World Wetlands Day 2025 was held.

question: The Bandipur Tiger Reserve is in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bandipur Tiger Reserve (बांदीपुर टाइगर रिजर्व) is located in the Chamarajanagar district of Karnataka, in the Western Ghats.

• It was established as a tiger reserve in 1973 under Project Tiger and is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

• It lies along the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu-Kerala tri-junction, adjoining Mudumalai, Wayanad and Nagarhole.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bandipur was once the private hunting ground of the Maharaja of Mysore.

• It is famous for tigers, elephants, gaur, sloth bears and sandalwood forests.

• Karnataka has several tiger reserves, including Bandipur, Nagarhole, Bhadra, Dandeli-Anshi and BRT.

NOTE

• Assam (Option 1): Home to Kaziranga and Manas tiger reserves, not Bandipur.

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): 'Tiger State' with Kanha, Bandhavgarh and Pench, but not Bandipur.

• Kerala (Option 4): Has Periyar and Parambikulam tiger reserves; Bandipur lies in Karnataka.

question: The operation of a satellite launch vehicle is based on which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Newton's third law of motion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A satellite launch vehicle (rocket) works on the principle of Newton's third law of motion (न्यूटन का गति का तृतीय नियम) — for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

• Hot gases are expelled downward at high speed (action), and the reaction thrust propels the rocket upward.

• This is fundamentally the principle of conservation of momentum.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The rocket's forward thrust equals the rate of change of momentum of the ejected exhaust gases.

• Newton's laws of motion were published in his work 'Principia Mathematica' (1687).

• India's launch vehicles include PSLV, GSLV and LVM3, operated by ISRO.

NOTE

• Newton's first law of motion (Option 1): The law of inertia; a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

• Newton's second law of motion (Option 2): Force equals rate of change of momentum (F = ma); explains how force changes motion.

• Archimede's principle (Option 4): Relates to buoyancy of objects in fluids, not rocket propulsion.

question: In 2024, which country became the first in the world to develop a wooden satellite named LignoSat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Japan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2024, Japan (जापान) became the first country in the world to develop a wooden satellite named LignoSat.

• It was developed by Kyoto University in collaboration with Sumitomo Forestry.

• The tiny satellite, made largely of magnolia wood, was designed to test wood's durability in space and reduce space debris/pollution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• LignoSat is a CubeSat about 10 cm on each side.

• Wooden satellites burn up cleanly on re-entry, avoiding harmful metallic particles in the atmosphere.

• It was carried to the International Space Station and deployed in orbit in late 2024.

NOTE

• Russia (Option 2): A major space power (Roscosmos), but did not build the first wooden satellite.

• China (Option 3): An advanced space nation, but not the developer of LignoSat.

• Israel (Option 4): Has a notable space program, but did not create the wooden satellite.

question:
Which of the following is an example of cooling due to evaporation?
I. Pouring of acetone on palm.
II. After a sunny day sprinkling water on roof.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Evaporation causes cooling (वाष्पीकरण के कारण शीतलन) because the liquid absorbs latent heat from its surroundings while turning into vapour.

• Pouring acetone on the palm feels cold because acetone evaporates quickly, taking heat from the skin (Statement I is correct).

• Sprinkling water on a hot roof cools it as the water evaporates and absorbs heat (Statement II is correct).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The heat absorbed during evaporation is called the latent heat of vaporisation.

• Faster-evaporating (volatile) liquids like acetone/ether produce a stronger cooling effect.

• The same principle explains sweating cooling the body and earthen pots keeping water cool.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete; sprinkling water on a roof also causes cooling by evaporation.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete; acetone on the palm also cools by evaporation.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both are valid examples of evaporative cooling.

question: In which of the following year the ruler of Iran, Nadir Shah, sacked and plundered the city of Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1739.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nadir Shah (नादिरशाह), the ruler of Iran (Persia), invaded India and sacked and plundered Delhi in 1739.

• He defeated the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah 'Rangila' at the Battle of Karnal (1739).

• He carried away enormous wealth, including the famous Peacock Throne (Takht-e-Taus) and the Kohinoor diamond.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The invasion caused a massacre in Delhi and severely weakened the already declining Mughal Empire.

• Nadir Shah founded the Afsharid dynasty of Persia and was assassinated in 1747.

• His invasion is often seen as a major blow that accelerated Mughal decline in the 18th century.

NOTE

• 1707 (Option 1): The year of Aurangzeb's death, marking the beginning of Mughal decline.

• 1728 (Option 2): No major Nadir Shah invasion of Delhi occurred in this year.

• 1751 (Option 4): After the sack of Delhi; not the year of Nadir Shah's invasion.

question: What was the new capital founded by Sawai Raja Jai Singh of Amber?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sawai Raja Jai Singh II of Amber founded the new capital city of Jaipur (जयपुर) in 1727.

• The city was designed by the architect/scholar Vidyadhar Bhattacharya on a planned grid pattern.

• Jaipur is known as the 'Pink City' and is today the capital of Rajasthan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jai Singh II was also a noted astronomer who built the Jantar Mantar observatories at Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura.

• The capital was shifted from Amber (Amer) to the newly built Jaipur.

• Jaipur, along with Amber, is part of Rajasthan's rich Rajput heritage and a UNESCO recognised city.

NOTE

• Udaipur (Option 2): Founded by Maharana Udai Singh II of Mewar (Sisodia dynasty).

• Jodhpur (Option 3): Founded by Rao Jodha of the Rathore dynasty in 1459.

• Ajmer (Option 4): An ancient city founded by the Chauhans, later a Mughal stronghold; not founded by Jai Singh.

question: In India, how many policy statements are mandated by the Fiscal responsibility and budget management act along with the budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 (वित्तीय उत्तरदायित्व और बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम) mandates that the government lay certain policy statements before Parliament with the budget.

• It originally required three policy statements: the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement, the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, and the Macroeconomic Framework Statement.

• These promote fiscal discipline, transparency and prudent debt management.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A fourth statement, the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement, is presented separately (in the session after the budget).

• The FRBM Act aims to reduce fiscal deficit and eliminate revenue deficit over time.

• The N.K. Singh Committee reviewed and recommended reforms to the FRBM framework.

NOTE

• Two (Option 1): Incorrect; the Act mandates three statements with the budget, not two.

• Five (Option 3): Incorrect number of mandated policy statements.

• Eight (Option 4): Incorrect; far more than the three required statements.

question: In which year was the Competition Act passed by the Parliament in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2002.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Competition Act (प्रतिस्पर्धा अधिनियम) was passed by the Parliament of India in 2002.

• It replaced the earlier MRTP Act (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969).

• The Act led to the establishment of the Competition Commission of India (CCI).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The CCI became fully functional around 2009 and works to prevent anti-competitive practices.

• The Act prohibits anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position and regulates combinations (mergers/acquisitions).

• It was amended notably in 2007 and again by the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.

NOTE

• 1998 (Option 1): Not the year the Competition Act was passed.

• 2004 (Option 2): Incorrect; the Act was enacted in 2002.

• 2000 (Option 3): Incorrect year for the Competition Act.

question: Which of the following crop is associated with dryland farming?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ragi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ragi (रागी), or finger millet, is associated with dryland (rainfed) farming as it grows well with limited water.

• Dryland farming (शुष्क खेती) is practised in areas receiving low rainfall (usually less than 75 cm) without assured irrigation.

• Crops like millets (ragi, bajra, jowar), pulses and oilseeds are typical dryland crops.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Millets are hardy, drought-resistant and rich in nutrients; 2023 was observed as the International Year of Millets.

• Ragi is widely grown in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

• Dryland/rainfed farming covers a large share of India's cultivated area.

NOTE

• Rice (Option 1): A water-intensive kharif crop requiring high rainfall or irrigation (wetland farming).

• Sugarcane (Option 2): A cash crop needing plenty of water and irrigation, not suited to dryland farming.

• Jute (Option 3): A fibre crop of hot, humid regions requiring abundant water, grown in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.

question: In which of the following valleys, over 97% of India's coal reserves are located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Damodar, Sone, Mahanadi and Godavari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Over 97% of India's coal reserves are located in the valleys of the Damodar, Sone, Mahanadi and Godavari (दामोदर, सोन, महानदी और गोदावरी) rivers.

• Most of this coal is of the Gondwana type, which forms the bulk of India's coal deposits.

• The Damodar valley is the most important coalfield region (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, etc.).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gondwana coal is about 250 million years old, while Tertiary coal is younger and found in the northeast.

• Major coal-producing States include Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh.

• India is among the largest coal producers and consumers in the world.

NOTE

• Ganga and Yamuna (Option 2): Fertile alluvial plains important for agriculture, not major coal reserves.

• Narmada and Tapi (Option 3): West-flowing rift-valley rivers of central India; not the main coal belt.

• Indus, Jhelum, Chenab and Sutlej (Option 4): Rivers of the northwestern Himalayan/Punjab region, not coal-bearing valleys.

question: As per Economic Survey 2023-24, it is expected that by 2030, more than ______ of India's population will live in urban areas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 40%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Economic Survey 2023-24 (आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण), it is expected that by 2030, more than 40% of India's population will live in urban areas.

• This reflects the rapid pace of urbanisation and its implications for infrastructure and employment.

• The Survey is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Economic Survey 2023-24 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman ahead of the Union Budget.

• The Chief Economic Adviser at that time was V. Anantha Nageswaran.

• Rising urbanisation requires investment in housing, transport, water and sanitation.

NOTE

• 50% (Option 2): Overstates the projected urban share for 2030.

• 55% (Option 3): Higher than the projected figure of over 40%.

• 60% (Option 4): Far higher than the Economic Survey's projection for 2030.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY)?
I. It is a Central Sector Scheme.
II. It is a Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) (राष्ट्रीय वयोश्री योजना) is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by the Central Government (Statement I correct).

• It is financed from the Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund, and the official key treats Statement II as correct as well.

• The scheme provides free assisted-living devices (aids and appliances) to BPL senior citizens.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• RVY is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

• Devices provided include walking sticks, hearing aids, wheelchairs, spectacles and dentures.

• It was launched in 2017 for senior citizens aged 60 years and above belonging to the BPL category.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete per the official key, which treats both statements as correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete; Statement I about it being a Central Sector Scheme is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as at least Statement I is definitely true.

question: As per MOSPI report of 2024, the female population of India by 2036 will be ______ of total population.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 48.8%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the MOSPI 'Women and Men in India 2024' (एम.ओ.एस.पी.आई. रिपोर्ट) report, the female population of India by 2036 is projected to be about 48.8% of the total population.

• This indicates a gradually improving sex ratio compared to earlier years.

• MOSPI is the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The report projects India's sex ratio to improve to around 952 females per 1000 males by 2036.

• 'Women and Men in India' is a flagship publication providing gender-disaggregated data.

• Such projections are based on the report of the Technical Group on Population Projections.

NOTE

• 41.8% (Option 2): Understates the projected female share of population.

• 53.8% (Option 3): Overstates the projected female population share.

• 51.8% (Option 4): Incorrect; the projected female share is about 48.8%, not a majority.

question: Which two causes did the Buddha identify as the roots of human suffering?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ignorance and Attachment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gautama Buddha identified Ignorance (अविद्या) and Attachment/desire (मोह/तृष्णा) as the roots of human suffering (dukkha).

• This forms part of the Four Noble Truths, where craving/attachment is the cause of suffering.

• Removal of ignorance and desire leads to liberation (nirvana).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Four Noble Truths (Arya Satya) are the core of Buddhist teaching.

• The path to end suffering is the Eightfold Path (Ashtangika Marga).

• Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and delivered his first sermon at Sarnath.

NOTE

• Hunger and Thirst (Option 1): Physical needs, not the philosophical roots of suffering in Buddhism.

• War and Poverty (Option 2): Social evils, but not identified by the Buddha as the fundamental causes of suffering.

• Violence and Disease (Option 4): Sources of pain, but not the Buddha's stated roots of dukkha.

question: Which ruler was the founder of the Nanda Dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahapadma Nanda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahapadma Nanda (महापद्मनंद) was the founder of the Nanda Dynasty (नंद वंश) of Magadha.

• He is described as 'Ekarat' (sole sovereign) and 'Sarvakshatrantaka' (destroyer of all Kshatriyas).

• He built a powerful empire with a large army in the 4th century BCE.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Nandas had their capital at Pataliputra.

• The last Nanda ruler was Dhanananda, who was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya with the help of Chanakya.

• The Nandas are known for their immense wealth and strong military.

NOTE

• Ashoka (Option 1): The great Mauryan emperor, grandson of Chandragupta Maurya; not a Nanda ruler.

• Dhanananda (Option 2): The last Nanda king, not the founder of the dynasty.

• Chandragupta Maurya (Option 4): Founder of the Maurya dynasty who overthrew the Nandas.

question: Which of the following is NOT a name used to refer to the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mesopotamian Civilization.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indus-Sarasvati Civilization is also known as the Harappan, Indus, or Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilization; Mesopotamian Civilization (मेसोपोटामिया सभ्यता) is NOT one of its names.

• Mesopotamia was a separate ancient civilization located between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers (modern Iraq).

• The Harappan civilization is named after Harappa, the first site excavated (1921).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilization (c. 2600-1900 BCE).

• It is called 'Sarasvati' because many sites lie along the dried-up Sarasvati (Ghaggar-Hakra) river bed.

• Major sites include Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, Lothal and Kalibangan.

NOTE

• Harappan Civilization (Option 1): A valid alternative name, derived from the site of Harappa.

• Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilization (Option 3): A valid name referring to the Indus (Sindhu) and Sarasvati river systems.

• Indus Civilization (Option 4): A commonly used name based on the Indus (Sindhu) river valley.

question: During the Gupta period, 'Bhagvatism', which emphasized bhakti and ahimsa, centered on the worship of which deity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishnu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the Gupta period, Bhagvatism (भागवतवाद) centered on the worship of Vishnu (विष्णु) and his incarnations (avatars).

• It emphasized bhakti (devotion) and ahimsa (non-violence) as paths to salvation.

• Vishnu was worshipped in the form of Vasudeva-Krishna, and the concept of avatars became popular.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Gupta age (c. 320-550 CE) is called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India.

• The Gupta kings were largely Vaishnavas and used titles like 'Parama Bhagavata'.

• Bhagavatism grew out of the earlier Bhagavata cult and later evolved into Vaishnavism.

NOTE

• Shiva (Option 1): Worshipped under Shaivism, a separate major sect, not the focus of Bhagvatism.

• Brahma (Option 3): The creator god of the Hindu trinity, but not the deity of Bhagvatism.

• Indra (Option 4): The Vedic king of gods and god of rain/thunder, not central to Gupta-era Bhagvatism.
